q: we introduce FrontierRefactor, a multi-scale benchmark of 60 qualified tasks across seven languages, four contract granularities, and two operational forms (in-place optimization and crosslanguage rewriting).
r: Include: new benchmark with new reference-free metrics (behaviour fidelity and speedup) for coding agents changing code across 1,080 runs; contribution is the evaluation method.

q: We study five questions. RQ1 (prevalence): how many required tests and milestones depend on unstated, non-inferable information?
r: Include: audits specification-oracle gaps in a feature-level milestone benchmark and their effect on agent scores; the contribution is the evaluation method.

q: we introduce SWE-Clar, a benchmark of 100 greenfield software development tasks based on real software development jobs on Upwork
r: Include: new benchmark where agents build greenfield applications from incomplete requirements, project level.

q: Each scenario combines an existing repository task with a task-relevant change introduced during execution.
r: EC6: scenarios are built on SWE-bench-style repository (issue repair) tasks, which are always excluded even with a method contribution.

q: three separate delegation studies with hidden behavioral checks
r: Include: experience report with multi-trial controlled comparisons of direct versus delegated coding with cost and verified success metrics.

q: We introduce FeatureLoop, a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks from 34 repositories across five primary programming languages and seven software forms.
r: Include: new benchmark for iterative feature development from evolving requirements, with cost and effort metrics and 12 models compared under one harness.

q: We ask whether this work needs dedicated orchestration and how such factories should be judged.
r: IC1: vision paper on orchestrating agent swarms for software maintenance, not evaluated; neither SDD, context files nor an evaluation or comparison of coding agents.

q: we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring, an open-ended task with no stopping criterion
r: Include: controlled multi-turn study of two agents and five models with repeated runs and new churn and quality metrics; the contribution is the study design.

q: We introduce FEATUREARC to evaluate coding agents on evolving features, together with a pipeline that constructs its tasks from repository histories.
r: Include: new benchmark at feature level with successive requirements, a new evaluation design and several agents compared.

q: we introduce CodeSpecWeave, a framework for synthesizing coding tasks with rich, interdependent specifications.
r: EC5: main contribution is a task-synthesis and RL training technique, tested on existing benchmarks, adding little to the evaluation method.
